# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-high

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Two cooperating agents (one per feature, with messaging and a shared git remote) run on the 50-pair `flash` subset with the exact same per-agent setup as [`solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-high`](../solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-high/summary.md): `gemini-3.8-flash` at `high` thinking, 500 steps, compaction at 64K tokens, the per-turn step counter, and a `$40` per-agent cost cap. Comparing against `solo` at `high` thinking (`34/50`, `$110.14`) and `coop` with shared git at `low` thinking ([`30/50`, `$39.85`](../coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-low/summary.md)) tests whether extra reasoning closes the 6-pair coordination gap seen at `low` thinking. It ran as two 25-pair halves on two API keys and was merged into this one run.

## Observations

- 34/50 (68%) for `$96.17`, matching `solo` at `high` thinking (`34/50`, 68%, `$110.14`) and up 4 pairs (+8 percentage points) from `coop` with shared git at `low` thinking (`30/50`, 60%, `$39.85`). Against `solo` at `high` thinking, the two runs agreed on 48 of 50 pairs: 33 passed in both, 15 failed in both, 1 passed only in `solo` (`pallets_click_task/2068` (6,7)), and 1 passed only in `coop` (`samuelcolvin_dirty_equals_task/43` (3,7), which neither `solo` `low` nor `solo` `high` solved).
- All 100 agents submitted well below the 500-step limit (median 104 steps, max 271, 0 at the limit), compacted a median of 3 times (vs. 7 in `solo` `high`, since each peer carries one feature instead of two), generated 7.3M reasoning tokens across the run (vs. 11.0M in `solo` `high`), exchanged 9 to 71 messages per pair (median 28.5), and merged without conflicts on all 50 pairs (46 clean three-way merges and 4 identical pre-merged branches).
- Compared with `coop` with shared git at `low` thinking (`30/50`), `high` thinking gained 5 pairs (`pallets_click_task/2068` (7,10), `pallets_click_task/2800` (2,7), `pallets_jinja_task/1621` (4,5), and both `samuelcolvin_dirty_equals_task/43` pairs (2,3) and (3,7)) and lost 1 (`pallets_click_task/2068` (5,11), which `solo` `high` also missed). Stronger per-agent reasoning eliminated single-feature state and edge-case bugs that slipped past trial merges at `low` thinking, such as preserving a context exit callback across reuse (`2800` (2,7)) and ignoring malformed priority entries (`1621` (4,5)).
- Even at `high` thinking, conflict-avoidance workarounds around shared call sites persisted. On both `pallets_click_task/2068` (7,10) and `pallets_click_task/2068` (6,7), the peers still agreed in chat to let only one agent add its new parameter to the shared constructor call line while the other agent assigned its setting as an attribute on the created instance afterward so `git merge` would stay conflict-free. On `(7,10)` that split happened to satisfy both hidden test suites because only the first feature's tests checked constructor arguments directly; on `(6,7)` the second feature's tests mocked the constructor and failed when its keyword argument was missing, accounting for the single pair `coop` `high` lost to `solo` `high`.
